name: The house: why, the bar, ideas, words

modules.title: Why before how
modules.need: New people learn the mechanics without the reason, and bend the standard under pressure
modules.roles: req All F; leaders first; BOH chef-gated form
modules.approach: Discussion. Founder-told on screen (recording or AI presenter, D4), then the learner explains one rule's reason aloud. Opens by normalizing struggle as common and temporary (Walton and Cohen, carried from the Learner Advocate profile); the ambition is framed as what the house builds with them, never a bar they are screened against. Carrier: commander's intent (ADP 6-0, VS), one spoken line at T0. Cite WP II "Onboarding" p.18; BG 01 "Company non-negotiables". The origin story goes to LIB-008 with the lineage flag; care moves to CUL-003
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can name the company non-negotiables and the order in which the house protects its people, and explain in their own words the reason behind one house rule and what they would act on when that rule no longer fits the moment.
teaches: Why the reason comes before the mechanics at Sŏn, and what that means for a new person's first weeks, framed as struggle that is common and temporary and a bar the house builds with them (WP Part II "Onboarding" p.18; Learner Advocate framing)
The company non-negotiables and the reason behind each (BG 01 "Company non-negotiables"; Tier 2 in BG 07)
The protection order (bandwidth, then joy, then retention, then results) and why the order is the decision (BG 01; WP Part I "What health looks like" p.12)
The front line as the most sensitive position, not the bottom of a hierarchy (WP Part I "The visual: the web" p.9)
Reading up the tiers to settle a conflict between rules (BG 07 "The six-tier authority hierarchy")
The house's intent in one spoken line, as what to act on when a rule no longer fits (commander's intent as carrier; the line itself from Brandon's interviews)
modules.leaves: The origin story and Brandon's own houses (LIB-008, lineage flagged); what the bar is and how it is judged (ORI-030); the detail behind the house's structural choices such as pay, strands and the overnight crew (ORI-022, whose one-line why sits inside this module); deciding from cases (ORI-003); the Korean terms and frameworks (ORI-007); care and its cost (CUL-003).
modules.proven: A short conversation before any customer contact: the person names the non-negotiables and explains the reason behind one house rule in their own words. No click-through release.
modules.waitsOn: Can be drafted now. The on-screen founder segment waits on Brandon recording it or consenting to an AI presenter (D4), and the intent line comes from his interviews (founder.*). The back-of-house form is chef-gated.
modules.recommendation: keep: the root of the trunk and the first star; every other module leans on it.

modules.title: What "best in the country" means and how it is judged
modules.need: People aim at good service because nobody has said what the top bar is, and cannot tell a peak night from consistency
modules.roles: req All F; Deep for leaders through ORI-031
modules.gate: T0 conversation: explain consistency over time in your own words
modules.approach: Discussion, one question: "which did we meet last night, and which did we only perform?" The public criteria of the Michelin Guide, including consistency between visits (VS), the James Beard Foundation's "consistent excellence in food, atmosphere, hospitality, and operations" and its values clause (VP), and Forbes Travel Guide's anonymous inspection against published service standards (VS), cited and never restated as house standards; never play to a guide's checklist (Goodhart). Brandon's own bar recorded through LIB-008, from his own account only. Absorbs ORI-025's core
modules.origin: RT best G9 · RT trad RT-03
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can say what bar Sŏn is aiming at, explain in their own words why consistency across nights and people counts for more than a peak night, and name how the country's top guides judge a restaurant without treating their criteria as the house standard.
teaches: Sŏn's aim to be one of the best restaurants in the country, and what Brandon means by it (from Brandon's interviews, recorded through LIB-008)
Consistency over time against the peak night: a standard met versus a standard performed (house framing; system-design teaching style)

How the top of the field is judged in public: the Michelin Guide's criteria including consistency between visits, the James Beard Foundation's "consistent excellence" criteria and values clause, Forbes Travel Guide's anonymous inspection against published standards (outside sources, cited, never restated as house standards)
Why the house never plays to a guide's checklist (Goodhart's law as the lens)
Why a late entrant aims at the definitive version of a known thing, not the first version of a strange one (WP "Sŏn is not a disruptor" passage p.35; the full episode lives in LIB-008)
modules.leaves: Holding the bar on an ordinary night after opening (ORI-031); the exact fixed standard (ORI-029, the standards book, D46); inspecting the house from the chair (LEA-045); Brandon's account of the houses that shaped him (LIB-008, from his own account, lineage flagged); how critics and inspectors are recognized (policy, D50).
modules.proven: A short conversation before customer contact: the person explains consistency over time in their own words and answers one question, which standard did we meet last night and which did we only perform.
modules.waitsOn: Brandon's statement of his own bar (founder.*, from his interviews). Guide criteria marked secondary are confirmed against the primary source before drafting.
modules.recommendation: keep: a distinct star (says what the bar is) and the anchor for ORI-031 and LEA-045.

modules.title: Two layers: service and hospitality, and the exact fixed layer
modules.need: People script where they should read the customer, improvise where the standard is fixed, and treat the fixed layer as approximate
modules.roles: req All customer-facing F; BOH know-only
modules.approach: Classification: contrast pairs of the same moment as checkable standard and as reading this customer; persona cases folded in from ORI-019 (BG 05 "calibrate, never constrain"). A third move added by the best-in-the-country read: the fixed layer is not only checkable, it is exact, and exactness is the care. Carrier: notes versus phrasing in music (principle). Cite BG 03 "This is not omotenashi"; BG 02 "Mahk"
modules.origin: Tr TR-01 · RT craft (ORI-019 folded) · RT best
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can sort a moment of service into the fixed layer (done exactly, the same every time) or the read layer (calibrated to this customer), and explain why the fixed layer is never approximate and the read layer is never scripted.
teaches: Service and hospitality as two layers of the same moment: the fixed, checkable standard and the reading of this customer (house framing; notes versus phrasing as carrier)
Why this is not omotenashi: anticipating and perfecting versus Jeong accumulating and Nunchi reading (BG 03 "Jeong and Nunchi", "A substantive distinction")
Exactness as care: the fixed layer is exact, not roughly right (house framing; the depth is in ORI-029)
Personas calibrate emphasis and never constrain: Mia, David, Clara, Marcus as contrast cases, and where each is lost (BG 05 "How they function", "Persona-to-daypart matrix")
Reads the system has already made: a protocol that is a system decision, never a floor call (BG 15 "Key protocols")
The specific over the generic in a moment (BG 02 "Mahk")
modules.leaves: Reading cues at a live table (SVC-006); the exact standards themselves (SVC-071, SVC-072, after the standards book, D46); the meanings of the Korean terms (ORI-007, founder.glossary); the smallest-task principle at depth (ORI-029); the beverage application (BEV-008).
modules.proven: A short conversation before customer contact, using contrast pairs: the person names which layer a moment belongs to and why.
modules.waitsOn: Nothing for the structure. Term meanings are founder.glossary bindings (D23) and persona-specific system steps are tool bindings.
modules.recommendation: keep: a distinct star (tells the fixed standard from the moment that calls for reading) and the prerequisite for SVC-006 and ORI-029.

modules.title: The ideas the house is built on
modules.need: People use the house's words as decoration, or gloss the Korean terms and persona labels wrongly, instead of using them as grounds for a decision
modules.cp: CP, T0 for the floor-minimum terms; T2 for the rest
modules.approach: Retrieval sets on the terms a person acts on in the first shifts; the rest spaced after release; a conversation applying one idea to a room moment. Meanings are founder.glossary.<term> (D23). Cite BG 02, BG 03 by label. The Eliasson carrier moves to ORI-026
modules.origin: Tr TR-02 · F · RT floor L4
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can name each house idea the floor acts on in the first shifts, state its meaning as Brandon's glossary sets it, and use one as the reason for a choice in a room moment.
teaches: The three cultural frameworks and why they hold veto power: Jaeyeonmi, Ma, Mahk, each with what it prohibits and requires (BG 02 "Three frameworks with veto power")
The bent spoon as the named forbidden category and the design target it sets (BG 02 "A named forbidden category")
The playground philosophy and its test, does this build or foreclose conditions for agency (BG 03 "Playground Philosophy")
Jeong, Nunchi and the persona labels as terms, with their meanings from Brandon's internal glossary, never the studio's gloss (BG 03, BG 05; founder.glossary.<term>, D23)
Code-bearing, not load-bearing: the system holds the knowledge and every role carries information (WP Part I "The engine: code-bearing vs. load-bearing" pp.7 to 8)
The one continuous arc: no daypart is a reset (BG 04 "The governing concept")
modules.leaves: Applying Jeong, Nunchi and the personas to service moments (ORI-006, SVC-006); the room's design decisions from Ma and Jaeyeonmi (ORI-010); daypart registers (ORI-020); Korean food culture (MNU-004); saying the terms to customers (ORI-009); the Eliasson carrier (ORI-026).
modules.proven: A short conversation before customer contact on the floor-minimum terms (apply one idea to a room moment), then a second conversation after release on the rest, with spaced recall between.
modules.waitsOn: Brandon's internal glossary of the Korean terms and persona labels (founder.glossary.<term>, D23).
modules.recommendation: keep: the vocabulary of reasons every other trunk module cites.

modules.title: How we talk here
modules.need: People carry industry vocabulary into the room, and use the other word for the customer
modules.approach: Spaced retrieval, spoken swap drills, a find-it card. Narrowed to the customer-facing lexicon and the one internal constant (customer, never the other word; BG 01 "Language constant"); the policing of second-language and code-switching speech between teammates is cut (RT floor). Cite BG 11 "Six rules", "Forbidden lexicon", "Preferred terms"; BG 06
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can swap any forbidden word for the house's preferred term while speaking, use the word customer without exception, and find a word's status on the card when unsure.
teaches: The language constant: customer, never the other word, in every context including internal talk (BG 01 "Language constant"; BG 06 "The six constants")
The forbidden lexicon, universal and in context, and why each word signals a brand performing itself (BG 11 "Forbidden lexicon")
The preferred terms in their four categories (BG 11 "Preferred terms")
The spoken register: present without performing, warmth in the attention not the adjective, specific over categorical, end at the last load-bearing word (BG 06 "The six constants"; BG 11 "Six rules")
We in the house's voice, you to the customer (BG 06; BG 11 "Customer relationship")
modules.leaves: Answering customers' questions about the house (ORI-009); the register of each daypart (ORI-020); the voice as an instrument (SVC-077); speech between teammates, including second languages and code-switching, which is not policed (cut by the floor red team).
modules.proven: A short conversation before customer contact with spoken swap items, then spaced recall. The find-it card is a job aid, not proof.
modules.recommendation: keep: short and concrete; it also carries the know-part of ORI-009 at the first conversation.

modules.title: Talking about the house honestly
modules.need: Novices improvise the concept story, over-claim, gloss terms wrongly, and fumble "can I tip?"
modules.cp: CP, T1 practice (know at T0 inside ORI-008)
modules.approach: Role-play on the questions customers actually ask, with a private first pass. founder.glossary.*, brand.*, founder.tipping_response. Cite BG 11 "Forbidden lexicon". No pay figures
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can answer the questions customers actually ask about Sŏn (what it is, a Korean term, can I tip) truthfully and in the house voice, without over-claiming, glossing a term wrongly, or explaining something to a customer who knows it better.
teaches: The concept in the house's approved words: one master brand, its dayparts at one address (BG 01 "The ecosystem"; the approved short version is brand.*)

The tipping question: why there is no tipping screen and the team's pay is built into the price, and the house's line in reply (BG 15 "Arrival"; WP Part II "How the team is paid" p.20; founder.tipping_response; no pay figures)
Korean terms in conversation: used without a gloss, and how to answer when asked (BG 09 "Hangul deployment"; founder.glossary, D23)
Not explaining to the customer who already knows (BG 05 Mia, "Fails when")
Names that are never said to a customer, such as late night's internal name (BG 01; BG 06)
Not over-claiming: no brand fact beyond canon, and finding out rather than guessing (brand.* bindings)
modules.leaves: Word swaps and the forbidden lexicon (ORI-008); dish and menu facts (MNU-001, chef); Korean food culture (MNU-004); the Korean drinks (BEV-028); the team-facing why of the pay model (ORI-022).
modules.proven: A role-play item in a short conversation after release to the floor, on real customer questions including the tipping one, after a private first pass.
modules.waitsOn: founder.tipping_response, founder.glossary (D23), and the approved concept story (brand.*).
modules.recommendation: keep: a performance skill (role-play) that ORI-008's word work does not cover.

modules.title: Why the house is built as it is, and how it knows it is working
modules.need: People read the house's unusual choices (pay built into the price, no tipping screen, the overnight crew, strands, paid learning, the cooling system) as quirks, and read measures as surveillance or play to participation
modules.cp: CP-short: the why at T0 inside ORI-001; the detail at T2
modules.unlock: H; the pay part after the transparency sheet exists (P)
modules.approach: Elaborative why prompt: explain one choice to a peer. Cite WP II "Labor as asset, not cost", "How the team is paid" p.20, "The cooling system"; WP pp.12, 22 to 23. Goodhart's law as a lens. Catubig post 1 on the cost of unpaid care. Never a persuasion piece standing in for a worker-auditable breakdown; never blame for labor cost. Conflict C15 (participation as a metric) to Brandon
modules.origin: Tr TR-30, TR-31 · RT craft (merge) · RT floor F-R4
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can explain to a peer the reason behind one of the house's unusual choices, and say what the house measures to know it is working and why a measure is a prompt to look, never a target.
teaches: Labor as an asset, not a cost, and the front line as the most sensitive position (WP Part II "Labor as asset, not cost" p.16)
The cooling system: burnout treated as a system failure, not a character flaw (WP Part II "The cooling system" pp.16 to 17)

How the team is paid, in principle only: built into the menu price, never a service charge, shared with the culinary team (WP Part II "How the team is paid" p.20); mechanics come from the transparency sheet (policy, D50; amounts fact.*)
Strands, not levels, and the overnight crew that frees servers for relationship work (WP Part I "The service team structure: complementary strands" pp.10 to 11; WP "The thank-you note" p.26)
Paid learning and why mastery, not completion, is what earns (WP Part II "Training infrastructure" pp.18 to 19; D6, D41)
How the house knows it is working: leading indicators and cultural impact measurement, read through Goodhart's law (WP Part II "Leading indicators" p.22, "Cultural impact measurement" p.23)
modules.leaves: The non-negotiables and the protection order (ORI-001, which also carries this module's one-line why at the first conversation); pay amounts and point mechanics (the transparency sheet, not instruction); private incident review (the LEA and CUL review modules); care and its cost (CUL-003); answering customers about tipping (ORI-009). The Coqodaq staffing comparison on WP p.22 is flagged for Brandon and not taught.
modules.proven: A short conversation item after release: the person explains one choice to a peer, with its reason.
modules.waitsOn: The transparency sheet (policy, D50) for the pay part; Brandon's call on conflict C15 (participation as a measure).
modules.recommendation: keep: the why is already inside ORI-001; this row carries the detail and the measures, which no other module holds.

modules.title: The standard lives in the smallest task
modules.need: People give care to visible moments and let unseen tasks slide (polishing, a set place, a clean edge); precision is treated as fussiness and the standard drifts from the edges in
modules.gate: T1 conversation: explain why one exact detail matters
modules.approach: Discussion with one demonstrated detail. Carriers: Guidara's rule that the right way starts with how you polish a wine glass (VP, transcript); Keller's finesse and urgency as preparation, not speed (VP, VS); Meyer's salt shaker, where drift is normal and re-centering is the leader's job (VS). One outside carrier for the novice test: a musician's intonation, one note flat in a chord
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can explain why one exact, unseen detail matters, show that detail done to the house standard, and name where drift starts.
teaches: No hierarchy of importance: every task held as equal, down to details most operators think beneath consideration (WP Part II "No hierarchy of importance" p.20)
Materials that ask for care, not concealment: evidence of time read as a feature, not a maintenance problem (BG 02 "Jaeyeonmi"; BG 13 "Materiality matrix")
Drift: how a standard slides from the edges in, and re-centering as the leader's job (Meyer's salt shaker as carrier)
Urgency as preparation, not speed, and the wine glass as where the right way starts (Keller and Guidara as carriers)
One demonstrated detail from the standards book (founder.standards_book, D46; the kitchen detail is chef)
modules.leaves: The drilled method for glass, silver and linen (SVC-071) and the place setting (SVC-072); the full standards book (D46); holding the bar on an ordinary night (ORI-031); the fixed-versus-read distinction itself (ORI-006).
modules.proven: A short conversation after release: the person explains why one exact detail matters, with the detail shown.
modules.waitsOn: The front-of-house half of the standards book (D46) for the demonstrated detail; the kitchen detail waits on the chef.
modules.recommendation: keep: its own star (holds the smallest task to the exact standard) and the gate before SVC-071 and SVC-072.

modules.title: Coming in with experience: what to keep, what to drop
modules.need: Experienced hires at every level bring another house's habits (scripted steps, rank displays, upselling reflexes, gatekeeping advancement) and read "why here" as "your past craft is wrong"; a one-size trunk bores or fails them
modules.roles: req All on the experienced path F; management bank req MD OM HB (was LEA-026)
modules.cp: CP on the experienced path, T0 to T1
modules.gate: placement conversation, then contrast cases; management bank proven with Brandon
modules.approach: Contrast-and-unlearn against BG 03 "This is not omotenashi" and BG 06, by label; Adrià's "creativity means not copying" as the frame for what to drop; ORI-003 at master depth for managers. Challenge invited through BEV-022's test-before-change rule. The unlearning claim is a hypothesis flagged for Brandon (the evidence concerns managers)
modules.origin: Ld NEW-L35 · Ho M-01 path · RT craft 2.7, 5 · RT floor (challenge route)
modules.afterThis: After this, an experienced hire can name which habits from another house to keep and which to drop at Sŏn, give the house's reason for each, and choose the challenge route for the units they already hold.
teaches: The house against the models people arrive with: this is not omotenashi, and the voice constants against industry habit (BG 03 "A substantive distinction"; BG 06)

Habits to drop, each against its house reason: scripted steps of service, rank displays, upselling reflexes, gatekeeping advancement (BG 15 "Step-back architecture"; BG 06 "Register by daypart"; WP Part I strands and "Advancement requires preparation, not permission" p.13)
What to keep, and how to challenge a house standard: test before change (BEV-022's rule; Adrià's "creativity means not copying" as the frame)
The challenge route: what can be proven by a spoken check or a banked run-through, and what is never challenged away (D39, D11)
Management bank: running a house that does not need the founder in the room (from Brandon's interviews; ORI-003 at depth)
modules.leaves: The decision casebook (ORI-003); management craft (LEA-027 intent, LEA-028 the parallel pair, LEA-029 owning the room); how readiness is proven (ORI-015); the beverage program's contrast (BEV-017). No contrast is drawn against Coqodaq, Alinea or Gracious practice; any such comparison is flagged for Brandon.
modules.proven: A placement conversation at entry, then contrast cases in a short conversation; the management bank is proven in conversation with Brandon.
modules.waitsOn: Brandon's interviews for the management bank and his call on the unlearning claim (flagged as a hypothesis); challenge specifics wait on the gate specs (D39).
modules.recommendation: keep: the only entry point for experienced hires and the door to the challenge route.

modules.title: Sit in the chair
modules.need: Team members have never received Sŏn's service, so they cannot see what their moves feel like
modules.roles: req All customer-facing W, recurring; porters and cooks by chef timing
modules.cp: CP, T2; a paid experience, not a module
modules.approach: The whole task before its parts. Design-research empathy; Rockwell (LO). Every new hire stays as a customer (Four Seasons, VS); founders ate in their own room as evaluation (EMP, VS). Recurring on workflow.staff_experience_cadence
modules.origin: Sv S28 · RT floor N6 · RT best G7 · RT craft
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can describe from the customer's seat how three of the house's moves felt (the threshold, the step-back, the close), and name one move of their own they would change because of it.
teaches: The spatial sequence lived as a customer, arrival to departure (BG 13 "The nine-beat spatial sequence")
The step-back felt from the chair: entry, delivery, exit (BG 15 "Step-back architecture")
The room's sound and light as received, not as specified (BG 13 "Lighting"; BG 14 "Curation and governance")
What to notice at the table and how to debrief it (design-research empathy as carrier)
modules.leaves: Leaders' structured inspection meals (LEA-045); reading the table (SVC-006); the room's intent (ORI-010).
modules.proven: A short conversation after the meal.
modules.waitsOn: The staff experience policy (founder.staff_experience_meal, D50) and its cadence (workflow.staff_experience_cadence); timing for cooks and porters is the chef's.
modules.recommendation: cut: as the card itself says, it is a paid house experience set by policy, not a module; keep the meal as a program mechanic beside LEA-045 and its debrief as a short conversation.

modules.title: House masterclass and the outside-field lens series
modules.need: Founder and partner conversations are lost to the team; recordings ramble; masterclasses are listened to, not worked
modules.approach: Recorded conversations plus "hosting the conversation" (interview craft from LEA-037). Episodes: the late entrant's advantage (was ORI-025; WP pp.35, 38 unverified at second hand; Coqodaq comparisons in WP pp.22, 31, 34 to 35 flagged), the origin story, Brandon's own bar. Lens series: one outside field per session plus one studio exercise. Jazz-style transcription: pull the moves from a founder conversation, name them, try them (Berliner, VS). workflow.recording_consent
modules.origin: 53 · Ld · X N24 · F P13 · RT floor (ORI-025 in)
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can pull the moves out of a recorded founder or partner conversation, name them, try one on shift, and host a recorded conversation so it is worked, not only listened to.
teaches: The founding episodes: the late entrant's advantage (WP p.35), the origin story, and Brandon's own bar (from Brandon's own account; lineage flagged)
Transcription: pull, name and try a master's moves (jazz transcription as carrier)
Hosting the conversation so it does not ramble (interview craft from LEA-037)
The lens series: one outside field per session, applied to Sŏn through its own lens, plus one studio exercise (system-design teaching style)
What is flagged and never taught as fact: the WP comparisons to Coqodaq (pp.22, 31, 34 to 35) and any practice of Brandon's lineage houses
modules.leaves: The bar itself (ORI-030); interview craft at depth (LEA-037); the reading tracks (other LIB rows).
modules.proven: A short conversation after an episode: the person names a move pulled from it and reports trying it.
modules.waitsOn: Brandon's recordings and workflow.recording_consent; the recording and hosting tool is a binding.
modules.recommendation: keep: the only route for founder knowledge into the library, and the source for ORI-030's bar.
